definitions.run_share: share of elapsed time spent running (moving and cadence ≥ 125 spm); stop = distance did not advance; walk = moving at cadence < 125
definitions.drift_pahr: Pa:HR drift = EF loss first→second half of a STEADY ≥ 45 min effort; null when not steady
definitions.fade: last vs first quarter of running seconds
definitions.hr_at_800: HR at 8:00/km on steady blocks, slope-corrected
definitions.evidence_tags: VALIDATED > MEASURED > CALCULATED > CLINICIAN > KB > REPORTED > LITERATURE > HYPOTHESIS

tasks.daily_brief: Give today's brief for a runner, in plain words. FIRST check context today_activity: when it exists the athlete has ALREADY trained today, so this is a post-run update, not a morning brief. Then the summary leads with what was done (distance, time, average HR, training load) and what it did to load (tsb_this_morning to tsb_after_today: form is yesterday's CTL minus ATL, so tsb_after_today is the form carried into tomorrow; below -30 means deep fatigue), and the call (see below) applies to the REST of today and to TOMORROW, not to the morning: say whether a second session today is not advised, what to do now (fuel, fluids, easy movement, sleep), and what tomorrow should be: compare today_activity.tomorrow_plan with the rules and say plainly KEEP, EASIER or SWAP/SKIP and why. Only existing rules force a change: pain 2/10 or more shortens or stops it, pain 4 or more means stop; a HARD planned session (quality, tt, speed, long, race) becomes easy when form after today is below -30 or ACWR is above 1.3; an EASY planned session is kept, with its heart-rate cap, unless pain applies; the final call is re-checked at tomorrow morning's sync (sleep HR above 67 or HRV reduced downgrades a hard session). Also say so if the planned week is above the +10 % load guard. Judge the run itself from its episode card and telemetry (pacing, HR drift, run share, heat) and say in one line if it matched the plan or the easy-HR cap. If today_activity is absent, write the normal morning brief. summary (max 2 sentences): start with the call in capitals, GO, EASY ONLY or REST, then the number that decides it, then today's session with its distance and heart-rate cap (the Z2 ceiling for easy running). The call comes ONLY from the locked rules (sleep HR above 67, HRV status reduced, pain 2/10 or more, red-flag symptoms), the readiness gate and the load guard; when another metric looks bad but no rule fires, keep the call and name it as a warning. analysis_md, three short sections (when today_activity exists the first one is '## Today's run and load' instead): '## The call' (the deciding numbers), '## Watch today' (at most 3 of: sleep HR vs 67, HRV vs baseline, pain, easy runs above the Z2 ceiling, HR at 8:00/km vs baseline, weekly km vs the +10 % guard, longest continuous run; each with its number and what would change the call; for HR at 8:00/km use twin.baselines.d30.hr_at_800, steady easy runs only, because twin.aerobic.hr_at_800 also counts races and run-walk sessions; if d30 has no value say it cannot be read yet), '## Data gaps' (only if one matters today, e.g. no pain check-in or the newest run has no FIT yet). recommendations: 1 to 3, the first is today's session with a concrete distance and heart-rate cap.
tasks.session_review: Coach this one session for a runner, not a scientist. STYLE OVERRIDES (they replace the ANALYSIS STRUCTURE above for this task): explain it the simplest way possible, like talking to a friend who just started running: short plain sentences, everyday words, NO jargon, NO metric abbreviations or acronyms (say 'your heart rate crept up late in the run' not 'Pa:HR drift'; 'you slowed down' not 'negative split failure'); every point must lead to something the runner can do. summary = HARD LIMIT 250 characters (it is shown as a preview): the verdict in one or two sentences plus the single most important next step. analysis_md = HARD LIMIT 2400 characters in total, exactly three short markdown sections: '## What went well' (max 3 bullets), '## What to watch' (max 2 bullets, only real concerns backed by the data), '## Next steps' (2-3 bullets: concrete next session, pace/heart-rate target, recovery or shoe/gym tweak). recommendations = 2 or 3 items only; each action is one short imperative sentence with a concrete number or day; why is at most one short sentence. flags = at most 2, only if something really needs attention. No repeating the same point across summary, analysis and recommendations.
tasks.weekly_review: Review the last week. Lead the summary with the call for next week, BUILD, HOLD or BACK OFF, and the numbers that decide it (weekly km vs the +10 % guard, pain events, readiness trend). Cover: easy-run discipline (easy runs above the Z2 ceiling, low-intensity share), HR at 8:00/km vs baseline (steady runs only: twin.baselines.d30.hr_at_800, not twin.aerobic, which includes races), durability (longest continuous run, fade onset), injury state, and the plan for the next week. recommendations: at most 3, each with a day and a number.
tasks.race_plan: Build or critique the race plan: opening cap, pacing by segment, heat and fuelling protocol, go/no-go gates.
tasks.question: Answer the question using the context.
